fields.description:
## Context / Problem
Store-wide maintenance walks visit every ticket directory on every run: the fsck scan loops (`_ticket_dirs` iterations in src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py) and the compact-all sweep (src/rebar/_commands/compact.py, whose per-ticket selection is `_scan_snapshot_state`'s own `os.scandir(tracker)` walk invoked by `compact_all_cli`) are O(all tickets ever created). As the store grows, archived tickets — cold, excluded from default `list` — dominate that walk and make routine health checks and sweeps slower for no operational value. `ticket list` already has the pattern to copy: default excludes archived (marker fast-path at reducer/_api.py with compiled-state confirmation) with an explicit `--include-archived` override.

## Approach
Two coupled changes, ordered so the default flip is safe:
1. **Operation-linked terminal fold.** Today `leaf.archive` (src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py) writes only the ARCHIVED event + `.archived` marker — it does NOT fold, so an archived ticket can carry unfolded tail events and the only thing that folds them is a later compact-all walk reaching it. Before scoping that walk to active tickets, make the fold part of the archive operation itself: `rebar archive` performs the ticket's final fold inline (reusing the existing single-ticket fold path compact_txn already exposes) right before writing the ARCHIVED event. This is operation-linked, so it is portable across environments with diverse or NO CI provider — no scheduled sweep is load-bearing. Any later `--include-archived` sweep becomes redundant belt-and-suspenders for tickets archived by pre-change builds, not the sole fold path.
2. **Active-only default scoping.** Introduce one shared helper (in the module fsck_scan already imports `_ticket_dirs` from) that yields ACTIVE ticket dirs by default — skipping dirs whose net archival state is archived, using the `.archived` marker as the fast-path and the existing `_is_net_archived`-style event-name confirmation, the exact semantics `list` uses — with an `include_archived` flag to yield everything. Switch the fsck scan loops to it, and in compact.py replace `_scan_snapshot_state`'s `os.scandir(tracker)` walk with the shared iterator (matching its existing return contract so `_foldable_event_count` consumers are unchanged), with `compact_all_cli` threading `--include-archived` through to it. Add `--include-archived` to `rebar fsck` and `rebar compact-all` (usage lines + JSON passthrough). Default = active-only for both: with change 1 in place, an archived ticket really IS folded on its way out, and any deep audit reaches it with the flag.
Back-out path: the default flip is a one-line revert per command (restore the full walk); change 1 is independently safe to keep since folding at archive time is strictly more converged than folding later.
Positive rationale: this reuses the archive marker + net-archival semantics that default `list` has proven, rather than inventing a second notion of active.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py — archive performs the ticket's terminal fold inline before the ARCHIVED event.
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py — scan loops take the shared active-only iterator; `include_archived` threading.
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py — CLI flag + usage + JSON passthrough.
- src/rebar/_commands/compact.py — `_scan_snapshot_state` replaces its `os.scandir` walk with the shared iterator; `compact_all_cli` threads `--include-archived` through; default active-only.
- tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py (new) — visited-set coverage both ways + archive-fold sequence test.
- docs/user-guide.md — document the default, the override, and the archive-time fold.

## Testing
- Happy path: fixture store with N archived (marker + ARCHIVED event) and M active tickets; default `rebar fsck` and `rebar compact-all --dry-run` visit exactly the M active dirs (assert on the visited set / reported counts); with `--include-archived` they visit N+M.
- Archive-fold sequence: archive a ticket that has unfolded events, then run DEFAULT `rebar compact-all`; assert the archived ticket's SNAPSHOT covers those events (nothing stranded) even though the default sweep never visited it — the fold happened at archive time.
- Edge: a ticket dir with a stale marker but NO net-archived state (reverted archive) is still visited by default (the confirmation step, not the marker alone, decides); an archived ticket with a corrupt event file IS reported when `--include-archived` is passed (deep audit still works); a ticket archived by a PRE-change build (unfolded, no inline fold) is folded by a `compact-all --include-archived` run (the belt-and-suspenders path works).
- Empty store: both commands succeed with zero visits.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar archive` folds the ticket inline (SNAPSHOT covers all its events) before writing ARCHIVED; a just-archived ticket followed by default `compact-all` carries no unfolded events; checked by the sequence test.
- [ ] Default `rebar fsck` and `rebar compact-all` visit only non-archived tickets, and `--include-archived` restores the full walk (including folding legacy archived-but-unfolded tickets); checked by the visited-set and legacy-fold tests.
- [ ] A reverted-archive ticket (stale marker) is never skipped by default; checked by the edge test.
- [ ] Usage lines and docs/user-guide.md name the new flag on both commands and the archive-time fold; checked by --help output in the test and the doc diff.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.
